A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VectorQ research. All main-text and appendix pages were readable, and visual inspection resolved extraction artifacts in figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original cache-hit, error-rate, latency, similarity-distribution, and sampling-ablation results in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original caching experiments across model configurations, repeated-run confidence intervals, latency measurements, and cache-size analysis in Section 6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The three-region cache logic and uncertainty gate remain. Explicit posterior-update calls in v2 Algorithm 1 were already described in v1. However, v1 Algorithm 2 specifies integral normalization, whereas v2 invokes max-normalization in a simplified proof and omits the update routine. Whether the actual posterior-update procedure changed is unresolved.

E1.justification: v1's benchmark combines E-Commerce, CommonsenseQA, Amazon Instant Video reviews, and ComQA, including distinct chatbot questions designed to prevent response reuse. v2 removes ComQA and this chatbot scenario from the revised benchmark definition, retaining classification and sentiment tasks. Larger sample counts do not add task coverage.

E2.justification: The static-threshold comparator and uniform-sampling ablation remain; v1 Figure 9 is retained as v2 Figure 18. v2 adds an explicit No Cache timing reference in its duration comparisons. Renaming the static comparator to State of the Art does not introduce another evaluated cache implementation.

E3.justification: The principal evaluations expand from 600 samples per configuration to 20,000 per individual dataset and 45,000 for the combined benchmark. v2 tests two embedding models with 8B and 70B LLMs, changes T4/Ollama serving to A100/vLLM, revises threshold and gate grids, and adds duration and precision–recall evaluation. The forced 300-miss/300-hit overhead protocol remains.

E4.justification: v1's aggregate similarity-density analyses using 400 samples are replaced by two embedding-specific cases drawn from a 45,000-prompt evaluation in v2 Figure 2. The learning curves in v1 Figure 5 disappear. v2 adds cache-hit latency versus cache-size analysis in Figure 7; the sampling ablation is retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run counts or confidence intervals. v2 Appendix D first reports three evaluations per VectorQ uncertainty-gate configuration, with 95% confidence intervals throughout the benchmark plots. This establishes a substantial reporting change, without establishing an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Benchmark results are extensively replaced and expanded under revised conditions. Reported headline benefits change from 12× cache hits and 92% error reduction to 26× and 74%. v2 adds duration, precision–recall, response-count, and cache-size results, including a 6-microsecond-per-MB latency slope. Figure 6's latency values and the sampling-ablation curves remain unchanged. The headline changes are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v1 Section 5.2 and Appendix D argue that the incorrect region converges to 1, permitting only perfect matches. v2 Section 5.3 instead defines threshold sequences and argues convergence to a general correctness boundary under independent sampling and full-support assumptions. It also adds posterior-convergence reasoning using discretization and a simplified kernel; several steps are explicitly informal.

C1.justification: The central claim that adaptive embedding-specific thresholds outperform static thresholds remains. v2 revises the claimed maximum benefits and narrows the stated empirical coverage from four datasets to three. Threshold convergence becomes more prominent in the abstract and contributions, but was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive limitation: character-level response matching can reject semantically equivalent chatbot answers and requires adaptation for such applications. It also discusses response metadata dominating cache memory and interprets threshold failure through differing embedding-specific boundaries. The earlier learning-curve interpretation is removed; embedding-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents model identifiers and embedding dimensions, GPU allocation and memory utilization, and response distributions in Tables 1–4. Conversely, v1's explicit posterior-update pseudocode and benchmark record schema/example are removed. These materially change reproducibility information without establishing removal of the posterior component itself.

R1.justification: The Related Work section is essentially unchanged. v2 adds Liu et al. (2024) to position the workloads around LLM-based relational queries and removes several references associated with omitted datasets, implementation choices, and posterior exposition, including Rogers et al., Ollama, and Schennach.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much core prose remain. v2 trims introductory examples, shifts terminology from Bayesian sampling toward correctness/uncertainty sampling, revises explanations and algorithm cross-references, creates a dedicated convergence subsection, and reorganizes the appendices around the expanded benchmarking material.

P2.justification: Benchmark displays are substantially redesigned into panels by model configuration, with confidence intervals and parameter annotations. v2 adds duration, precision–recall, cache-size plots, and four response-distribution tables; it replaces Figure 2 and removes the learning and aggregate-density figures. The architecture and ablation figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Larger evaluations across model combinations, repeated-run confidence intervals, duration comparisons, and cache-size measurements strengthen v1's limited empirical support. The explicit response-matching limitation also improves scope qualification. Gains are tempered by lost posterior-update detail and chatbot coverage, a partly informal convergence argument, and reporting inconsistencies: v2 Figure 5 labels as Amazon reviews the plot repeated under E-Commerce in Figure 15, while equal-response balancing claims conflict with Tables 1–2.
